ran.title: 然 combos
ran.subtitle: The 然 family sorted out — the ones that look alike and mean different things.

groups.label: 突发 · All of a sudden

items.note: Concedes a fact you are about to push back against. Chinese keeps both halves — 虽然 in the first clause, 但是 or 可是 in the second — where English drops one of them.
items.example: 虽然很累，但是我还是把作业写完了。
items.example_pinyin: Suīrán hěn lèi, dànshì wǒ háishi bǎ zuòyè xiě wán le.
items.example_translation: Although I was shattered, I still finished the homework.

items.note: The mirror of 虽然. 虽然 concedes a fact and then argues against it; 既然 takes a fact as settled and draws a conclusion from it, usually with 就 in the second clause.
items.example: 既然你不舒服，就早点回家吧。
items.example_pinyin: Jìrán nǐ bù shūfu, jiù zǎodiǎn huí jiā ba.
items.example_translation: Since you're not feeling well, go home early.

items.note: Puts events in time order. In actual speech it is also the great filler — people string whole stories together on 然后…然后…, much like English "and then".
items.example: 我先去买菜，然后回家做饭。
items.example_pinyin: Wǒ xiān qù mǎi cài, ránhòu huí jiā zuò fàn.
items.example_translation: I'll do the shopping first, then go home and cook.

items.note: The written cousin of 但是. Fine in an essay or a news piece; saying it out loud over dinner sounds like you are reading from a script.
items.example: 他很努力，然而结果并不理想。
items.example_pinyin: Tā hěn nǔlì, rán'ér jiéguǒ bìng bù lǐxiǎng.
items.example_translation: He worked hard; the result, however, was disappointing.

items.note: Sets up the consequence of not doing the thing. Usually a warning.
items.example: 快走吧，不然就迟到了。
items.example_pinyin: Kuài zǒu ba, bùrán jiù chídào le.
items.example_translation: Get a move on, or we'll be late.

items.note: Softer and chattier than 不然, and it can open a suggestion rather than a threat — closer to "or we could just…".
items.example: 要不然我们改天再去？
items.example_pinyin: Yàobùrán wǒmen gǎitiān zài qù?
items.example_translation: Or shall we just go another day?

items.note: Agreement with no hesitation in it. On its own, 当然 answers a question the way "of course" does in English.
items.example: 当然可以，你随时来。
items.example_pinyin: Dāngrán kěyǐ, nǐ suíshí lái.
items.example_translation: Of course — come round whenever.

items.note: Confirms a prediction: you called it, and it happened. The exact opposite of 竟然 and 居然, which mark the thing you did not see coming.
items.example: 我就说他会迟到，果然又迟到了。
items.example_pinyin: Wǒ jiù shuō tā huì chídào, guǒrán yòu chídào le.
items.example_translation: I said he'd be late, and sure enough he was late again.

items.note: Marks something contrary to what you assumed, often with a note of disapproval. Very close to 居然 — 竟然 leans slightly more written and slightly cooler.
items.example: 他竟然一句话都没说就走了。
items.example_pinyin: Tā jìngrán yí jù huà dōu méi shuō jiù zǒu le.
items.example_translation: He actually left without saying a single word.

items.note: The stronger, more spoken twin of 竟然. Carries real surprise — either admiration or outrage, depending on tone.
items.example: 这么难的题他居然做出来了。
items.example_pinyin: Zhème nán de tí tā jūrán zuò chūlái le.
items.example_translation: He actually solved it — a problem that hard!

items.note: Says the evidence makes something plain. It is about what anyone can see, not about how sure you personally feel — that is 肯定.
items.example: 他显然还没准备好。
items.example_pinyin: Tā xiǎnrán hái méi zhǔnbèi hǎo.
items.example_translation: He's clearly not ready yet.

items.note: Formal and a bit weighty — commentary and argument rather than conversation, where you would just say 一定.
items.example: 这种做法必然会失败。
items.example_pinyin: Zhè zhǒng zuòfǎ bìrán huì shībài.
items.example_translation: An approach like that is bound to fail.

items.note: Worth keeping apart from 偶尔. 偶尔 is about frequency ("now and then"); 偶然 is about cause ("as it happened, by chance").
items.example: 我们是在一次会议上偶然认识的。
items.example_pinyin: Wǒmen shì zài yí cì huìyì shàng ǒurán rènshi de.
items.example_translation: We met by chance at a conference.

items.note: Same job as 仍然, but with a touch of feeling to it — the sense that time has passed and something has held on regardless.
items.example: 十年过去了，这家店依然开着。
items.example_pinyin: Shí nián guòqù le, zhè jiā diàn yīrán kāizhe.
items.example_translation: Ten years on, the shop is still open.

items.note: The neutral, factual one. Reports that a state has not changed, without any warmth attached.
items.example: 问题仍然没有解决。
items.example_pinyin: Wèntí réngrán méiyǒu jiějué.
items.example_translation: The problem still hasn't been resolved.

items.note: The everyday one, and the only one here that also works as an adjective — 很突然, 太突然了 are all fine.
items.example: 他突然站起来走了。
items.example_pinyin: Tā tūrán zhàn qǐlái zǒu le.
items.example_translation: He suddenly stood up and left.

items.note: Adverb only — 很忽然 is not a thing. Otherwise interchangeable with 突然 before a verb.
items.example: 天忽然下起了大雨。
items.example_pinyin: Tiān hūrán xià qǐ le dàyǔ.
items.example_translation: All at once it started pouring.

items.note: Sudden *and* forceful. Use it for a physical jerk of movement rather than for news arriving out of nowhere.
items.example: 他猛然回头，吓了我一跳。
items.example_pinyin: Tā měngrán huítóu, xià le wǒ yí tiào.
items.example_translation: He whipped round and gave me a fright.

items.note: Doubles as the noun "nature". As a manner word it means unforced — the opposite of stiff or performed, which is why it sits close to 松弛感.
items.example: 放松点，表现得自然一点。
items.example_pinyin: Fàngsōng diǎn, biǎoxiàn de zìrán yìdiǎn.
items.example_translation: Relax a bit — act more naturally.

items.note: Almost always followed by a negative — 全然不顾, 全然不知. Rarely used to intensify anything positive.
items.example: 他全然不顾别人的感受。
items.example_pinyin: Tā quánrán búgù biérén de gǎnshòu.
items.example_translation: He pays absolutely no regard to how anyone else feels.

items.note: The look on your face when nothing has landed. Often 一脸茫然 — "a face full of blank".
items.example: 听完他的解释，我还是一脸茫然。
items.example_pinyin: Tīng wán tā de jiěshì, wǒ háishi yì liǎn mángrán.
items.example_translation: After his explanation I was still completely blank.

items.note: Almost never stands alone — you will meet it as 恍然大悟, the moment the penny drops.
items.example: 经他一说，我恍然大悟。
items.example_pinyin: Jīng tā yì shuō, wǒ huǎngrán dàwù.
items.example_translation: One remark from him and it all clicked.

items.note: Not relief from danger but relief from a knot in your head — you have finally made peace with something that was nagging.
items.example: 想通之后，他终于释然了。
items.example_pinyin: Xiǎng tōng zhīhòu, tā zhōngyú shìrán le.
items.example_translation: Once he'd worked it through, he finally felt at peace with it.

items.note: Taking something calmly, almost coolly. The temperament behind 松弛感 — praise or an insult depending on what you stayed calm about.
items.example: 面对批评，她显得很淡然。
items.example_pinyin: Miàn duì pīpíng, tā xiǎnde hěn dànrán.
items.example_translation: She took the criticism completely in her stride.

items.note: Composed because you have nothing to hide. 淡然 is not minding; 坦然 is facing it squarely.
items.example: 他坦然承认了自己的错误。
items.example_pinyin: Tā tǎnrán chéngrèn le zìjǐ de cuòwù.
items.example_translation: He owned up to his mistake without flinching.

items.note: Lives in two set phrases: 截然不同 (completely different) and 截然相反 (the exact opposite). Rarely seen anywhere else.
items.example: 两个人的性格截然不同。
items.example_pinyin: Liǎng gè rén de xìnggé jiérán bùtóng.
items.example_translation: The two of them have completely different temperaments.

utterances.title: 口头禅 · Utterance glossary
utterances.subtitle: The connective tissue of real speech — what people actually say to start, join and close what they're saying.

items.note: Pure hesitation noise — buys you a second while you find the word, or eases into something slightly awkward. One of the most common things you'll hear and one of the last things textbooks teach.
items.example: 那什么…我先走了啊。
items.example_pinyin: Nà shénme… wǒ xiān zǒu le a.
items.example_translation: Um… I'm going to head off.

items.note: Flags that something worth hearing is coming and claims the floor for a moment. Warm rather than bossy between friends.
items.example: 我跟你说，这家店真的绝了。
items.example_pinyin: Wǒ gēn nǐ shuō, zhè jiā diàn zhēn de jué le.
items.example_translation: Listen, this place is unreal.

items.note: Drops out of joking register into something sincere. Often follows a run of banter to signal the joking has stopped.
items.example: 说真的，你该休息了。
items.example_pinyin: Shuō zhēn de, nǐ gāi xiūxi le.
items.example_translation: Seriously though, you need to rest.

items.note: Opens a mild disagreement. The 吧 is doing the work — it turns a flat correction into something tentative and much easier to take.
items.example: 其实吧，我觉得没那么严重。
items.example_pinyin: Qíshí ba, wǒ juéde méi nàme yánzhòng.
items.example_translation: Actually, I don't think it's that bad.

items.gloss: and then? / and your point is?
items.note: As a question it keeps someone's story moving. Said flat, with the stress landing on 呢, it turns sarcastic — "and so what?"
items.example: ——他就直接走了。——然后呢？
items.example_pinyin: —Tā jiù zhíjiē zǒu le. —Ránhòu ne?
items.example_translation: "And he just walked off." "And then?"

items.note: Restates what was just said, either to check you've understood or to put your own point more plainly. 也就是说 is the slightly fuller version.
items.example: 就是说，你今天来不了了？
items.example_pinyin: Jiùshì shuō, nǐ jīntiān lái bu liǎo le?
items.example_translation: So basically, you can't make it today?

items.note: Buys thinking time before something delicate, and warns the listener that what's coming is complicated or unwelcome.
items.example: 怎么说呢，这事儿有点复杂。
items.example_pinyin: Zěnme shuō ne, zhè shìr yǒudiǎn fùzá.
items.example_translation: How do I put this — it's a bit complicated.

items.note: Pivots back towards the other side of an argument, usually to be fair to someone you have just been criticising.
items.example: 话说回来，他也不容易。
items.example_pinyin: Huàshuō huílái, tā yě bù róngyì.
items.example_translation: Then again, he hasn't had it easy either.

items.note: Waves away the detail and cuts to what holds regardless. Can sound breezy or slightly stroppy depending on tone.
items.example: 反正我不去，你们玩得开心。
items.example_pinyin: Fǎnzhèng wǒ bú qù, nǐmen wán de kāixīn.
items.example_translation: Anyway, I'm not going — have fun without me.

items.note: Sets up the punchline of an anecdote. The 呢 holds a beat of suspense before you deliver it.
items.example: 我等了两个小时，结果呢，他忘了。
items.example_pinyin: Wǒ děng le liǎng gè xiǎoshí, jiéguǒ ne, tā wàng le.
items.example_translation: I waited two hours and — get this — he'd forgotten.

items.note: Announces that you are about to drop the polite framing and name the real issue.
items.example: 说白了，就是钱的问题。
items.example_pinyin: Shuōbáile, jiùshì qián de wèntí.
items.example_translation: Put bluntly, it comes down to money.

items.note: Friendly disbelief — you don't buy what someone just said. Fine with mates, sharp with a stranger.
items.example: 得了吧，你上次也这么说。
items.example_pinyin: Déle ba, nǐ shàng cì yě zhème shuō.
items.example_translation: Come off it, you said that last time too.

items.note: Looks like a negative and means the opposite — wholehearted agreement. A rhetorical "isn't that just the truth".
items.example: ——今年太热了。——可不是嘛！
items.example_pinyin: —Jīnnián tài rè le. —Kě bùshì ma!
items.example_translation: "It's been so hot this year." "Tell me about it!"

items.note: Despite meaning "don't say", it concedes that someone has a point — usually one you didn't expect to agree with.
items.example: 你别说，这么一改还真好看。
items.example_pinyin: Nǐ bié shuō, zhème yì gǎi hái zhēn hǎokàn.
items.example_translation: You know what, it actually does look better like that.

items.gloss: surely not, that's a bit much
items.note: Pushes back on an overreaction — you think someone is taking it further than the situation warrants.
items.example: 不至于吧，有那么夸张吗？
items.example_pinyin: Bù zhìyú ba, yǒu nàme kuāzhāng ma?
items.example_translation: Surely not — is it really that dramatic?

items.note: A knowing wink that skips the explanation, usually because saying it outright would be indiscreet.
items.example: 他为什么升职，你懂的。
items.example_pinyin: Tā wèishéme shēngzhí, nǐ dǒng de.
items.example_translation: Why he got promoted — well, you know.

items.gloss: I reckon, way I see it
items.note: Northern and folksy. Went meme-ish online, so younger speakers often use it with a knowing grin rather than straight.
items.example: 我寻思这事儿不太对啊。
items.example_pinyin: Wǒ xúnsi zhè shìr bú tài duì a.
items.example_translation: Way I see it, something's off here.

items.note: Another northern emphatic yes that is shaped like a no. Punchier and more regional than 可不是嘛.
items.example: ——他厨艺不错。——那可不！
items.example_pinyin: —Tā chúyì búcuò. —Nà kě bù!
items.example_translation: "He's a decent cook." "Too right he is!"

items.note: The polite dodge. 那个 stands in for the word that would be rude to say — a bit much, a bit off, a bit odd.
items.example: 他说话有点那个，你别介意。
items.example_pinyin: Tā shuōhuà yǒudiǎn nàge, nǐ bié jièyì.
items.example_translation: He's a bit… you know, when he talks. Don't take it to heart.

items.gloss: not that I'm one to talk, but
items.note: A pre-apology bolted onto criticism you fully intend to deliver anyway.
items.example: 不是我说，你这字也太潦草了。
items.example_pinyin: Bùshì wǒ shuō, nǐ zhè zì yě tài liáocǎo le.
items.example_translation: Not that I'm one to talk, but your handwriting is a disgrace.

items.note: The 吧 turns a firm opinion into a tentative one, leaving room for the other person to disagree without a row.
items.example: 我觉得吧，还是再等等比较好。
items.example_pinyin: Wǒ juéde ba, háishi zài děngdeng bǐjiào hǎo.
items.example_translation: Personally, I'd rather we waited a bit longer.

items.note: Drops the matter — sometimes generous, sometimes resigned, occasionally passive-aggressive. Tone decides which.
items.example: 算了，不说这个了。
items.example_pinyin: Suànle, bù shuō zhège le.
items.example_translation: Never mind, let's drop it.

items.note: Reluctant acceptance. 行 alone is a clean yes; adding 吧 makes it an audible sigh.
items.example: 行吧，那就听你的。
items.example_pinyin: Xíng ba, nà jiù tīng nǐ de.
items.example_translation: Fine, we'll do it your way then.

items.note: The standard way to wind up a call or a thread without anything being wrong.
items.example: 那就这样吧，回头再聊。
items.example_pinyin: Nà jiù zhèyàng ba, huítóu zài liáo.
items.example_translation: Let's leave it there — talk soon.

items.gloss: that's enough now, knock it off
items.note: Tells someone they have taken it far enough. Blunt but not vicious — the register of an exasperated friend.
items.example: 差不多得了啊，别闹了。
items.example_pinyin: Chàbuduō déle a, bié nào le.
items.example_translation: All right, that's enough — pack it in.
